headline: Former MP Bodi and 3 army officials sent to jail in Ekram murder case
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has ordered the detention of four accused, including former MP Abdur Rahman Bodi, over the 2018 killing of Teknaf councillor Ekramul Haque.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has sent former Cox's Bazar-4 MP Abdur Rahman Bodi and three retired army officials to jail. They were produced before the court today after arrest warrants were issued against them.
The other detained officials are retired Colonel Mohammad Anwar Latif Khan, Brigadier General Mahbub Alam, and Brigadier General Miftauddin Ahmed.

The case involves the 2018 killing of Teknaf councillor Ekramul Haque. According to the prosecution, Ekramul was picked up from a road in Teknaf on May 26, 2018, and killed in an alleged staged gunfight.
The tribunal has also ordered notices to be published in two newspapers for seven fugitive accused, including ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan.

Other fugitives include former road transport and bridges minister Obaidul Quader and former IGP Benazir Ahmed. The prosecution has accused the 11 individuals of unlawful detention, abduction, and ordering the murder.
The court has fixed September 7 for the next hearing in the case.
caption:
Former MP Abdur Rahman Bodi and three retired army officials are now behind bars over the 2018 killing of a Teknaf councillor.

The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has sent former Cox's Bazar-4 MP Abdur Rahman Bodi and three retired army officials to jail. They were produced before the court today after arrest warrants were issued against them.

The other detained officials are retired Colonel Mohammad Anwar Latif Khan, Brigadier General Mahbub Alam, and Brigadier General Miftauddin Ahmed.

The case involves the 2018 killing of Teknaf councillor Ekramul Haque. According to the prosecution, Ekramul was picked up from a road in Teknaf on May 26, 2018, and killed in an alleged staged gunfight.

The tribunal has also ordered notices to be published in two newspapers for seven fugitive accused, including ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan.

Other fugitives include former road transport and bridges minister Obaidul Quader and former IGP Benazir Ahmed. The prosecution has accused the 11 individuals of unlawful detention, abduction, and ordering the murder.

The court has fixed September 7 for the next hearing in the case.

headline: AB de Villiers backs Bangladesh to put up a good fight in South Africa
summary: The South African legend believes the Tigers can be competitive in the upcoming tour, provided their batters adapt to the challenging seaming conditions.
details: South Africa legend AB de Villiers believes Bangladesh can put up a strong fight on their upcoming Test tour of South Africa, despite the demanding conditions.
Bangladesh are scheduled to tour South Africa in November for two Test matches, three ODIs, and three T20Is.
De Villiers noted that South African pitches are among the toughest in the world for batters, as the ball not only swings after pitching but also moves off the seam.
He advised the Bangladeshi batters to be proactive rather than simply trying to survive, suggesting strategies like coming down the crease or adjusting how they cover their stumps.
The confidence comes as Bangladesh has already secured Test wins in Australia and New Zealand, leaving South Africa and India as the only two teams they haven't yet won against in Tests.
The first Test will be played in Johannesburg from November 15 to 19, and the second in Centurion from November 23 to 27.
caption:
Can the Tigers conquer South Africa? AB de Villiers thinks they can.

South Africa legend AB de Villiers believes Bangladesh can put up a strong fight on their upcoming Test tour of South Africa, despite the demanding conditions.

Bangladesh are scheduled to tour South Africa in November for two Test matches, three ODIs, and three T20Is.

De Villiers noted that South African pitches are among the toughest in the world for batters, as the ball not only swings after pitching but also moves off the seam.

He advised the Bangladeshi batters to be proactive rather than simply trying to survive, suggesting strategies like coming down the crease or adjusting how they cover their stumps.

The confidence comes as Bangladesh has already secured Test wins in Australia and New Zealand, leaving South Africa and India as the only two teams they haven't yet won against in Tests.

The first Test will be played in Johannesburg from November 15 to 19, and the second in Centurion from November 23 to 27.
